subject: EU region elevated p95 latency — customer advisory and follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@apexai.com>, Apex AI Support <support@apexai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU region elevated p95 latency — customer advisory and follow-up

Hi Lena / Apex team,

Quick heads-up: we detected an elevated p95 for hosted inference calls originating from eu-west-1 starting ~2026-08-01 08:45 UTC. Baseline p95 for the model family you run is ~160ms; we've observed spikes up to ~1.1s for several routes (generation and chat completions).

What we're doing now:
- Incident page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/EU-P95-20260801 (live updates).
- Short-term mitigation: traffic steering to nearby regions and a controlled increase in worker batch window to relieve queue pressure.
- Investigation focus: autoscaler-prediction delta combined with a recent routing policy change introduced this morning.

Impact for you: some requests may see delayed p95 and occasional timeouts. We have routed ~35% of your traffic to eu-central while we stabilize. No data loss; requests are queued and retried per your configured retry policy.

Attachments: p95_snapshot_20260801.csv (sample telemetry for affected hosts).

I'll send updates as we get stable improvements. If you need us to reroute all traffic to a specific region or pin a model variant for a short window, tell me which cluster and I'll coordinate.

Sorry for the disruption — we'll keep this short and focused.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

2) ETA on when p95 is expected back to baseline (or next update cadence)?

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU region elevated p95 latency — customer advisory and follow-up

Hi Lena — quick update and answers inline.

On model impact: affected traffic was primarily hitting redwood/gpt-legacy-v2 and redwood/chat-mid-1 in eu-west-1. We confirmed the routing change applied a weighting tweak this morning that concentrated short-lived high-concurrency requests onto fewer worker pools. That, combined with a kernel fallback on two host families, caused more frequent KV cache evictions and longer per-token stalls.

Mitigations performed (11:00 UTC):
- Rebalanced steering weights to smooth request distribution (rolled back the morning change).
- Temporarily widened batching window for gen/chat routes that are latency-tolerant.
- Forced rolling restart on the two host families with kernel fallback.

Observed effect: p95 for affected routes decreased from ~1.1s to ~220ms within 20 minutes. We're continuing to monitor; traffic is still partially routed to eu-central as a safety measure.

ETA & cadence: we'll post interim telemetry at +2h and +4h, and provide a post-incident summary by EOD. If you want us to fully evacuate eu-west for your account while we finalize the patch, confirm and we'll schedule a short planned switch (possible additional cross-region latency).

Attachment: p95_snapshot_20260801.csv (attached sample timeframe 08:30–11:00 UTC).

Connor O'Brien
Incident Response Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@apexai.com>, Apex AI Support <support@apexai.com>, ops@apexai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T16:38:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — EU p95 event (2026-08-01)

Lena / Apex ops —

Summary (final):
- Incident window: 2026-08-01 08:45 UTC — 2026-08-01 12:10 UTC (stabilized; monitoring continues).
- Root cause: a regression in a traffic-steering policy deployed at 08:12 UTC that unintentionally concentrated bursty short-lived requests onto a subset of worker pools, exposing a kernel-level fallback that increased KV cache eviction rates and amplified queueing.
- Impact: elevated p95 (up to ~1.1s) and intermittent timeouts for streaming generation routes in eu-west-1.

What we changed:
1) Rolled back the steering policy and rebalanced weights.
2) Fixed the autoscaler threshold misconfiguration to prevent under-provisioning on bursty workloads.
3) Deployed kernel patch to eliminate the fallback path; scheduled a controlled re-roll for the host families.
4) Added a targeted pre-warm job for high-concurrency routes and will maintain it for the next 48 hours.

Customer remediation offer: we can apply a one-time service credit for the affected window; if you'd like that applied to the account we will process it once you confirm the billing contact.

Next steps (internal & shared):
- Draft postmortem (internal) — https://drive.redwood.com/teams/infra/postmortem/EU-P95-20260801 (redwood_postmortem_draft.pdf attached).
- Follow-up action items: steering-policy unit tests, autoscaler e2e tests, and a post-deploy smoke-check pipeline for eu-west changes.
- We'll run a joint postmortem call if you'd like; proposed times: tomorrow 09:00–10:00 UTC or tomorrow 15:00–16:00 UTC.

Please reply if you'd like the full traffic evacuation to run now, to take the service credit, or to schedule the postmortem call. Thanks again for your patience — we're making changes to reduce the likelihood of recurrence.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood_postmortem_draft.pdf (postmortem draft, internal notes removed in shared copy).
